subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you earlier. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we stay aligned: 

Recap from today's discovery call:
- Current usage: ~50M tokens/month (mainly generation), embeddings ~5M/month.
- Forecast: 200M tokens/month steady-state within 12 months (higher peak Q4).
- Primary workloads: short-form generation (agent responses) ~75% tokens, embeddings for search ~25%.
- Success criteria: maintain latency <200ms p50 for short multi-turn responses and hit target unit economics.

Cost/price items we need from you to finalize a first commercial:
1) Confirm target $/1M tokens you have in mind (you mentioned a target around mid-$40s on the call).
2) Procurement preferences (12-month reserved commit vs month-to-month).
3) Any compliance/contract must-haves (SOC 2 evidence already helpful).

For context and benchmarking (preliminary):
- OpenAI hosted (latest generation) equivalent workloads often price in the high $100s per 1M tokens for advanced models; hosted rates for base models can be lower but still materially above open-model hosts for high-volume generation.
- Anthropic hosted rates are similar band for Claude-family production endpoints.
- Open-model hosts (self-hosted/managed on quantized models) tend to land lower — in the $20–$80 per 1M token range depending on model/quantization and whether you take Dedicated/Reserved capacity.

Next steps (proposed):
- Alex to confirm target $/1M for generation and embeddings and preferred commit term (reply to this thread).
- We'll scope a commercial (price bands + reserved capacity options) and share a short pricing teaser + sample MLP (mutual action plan) by EOD Friday.

Attaching a one-pager that summarizes our typical economics and two benchmark scenarios (hosted vs dedicated).

Thanks — talk soon.
— Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-teaser.pdf (1 page)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Thanks Vanessa — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Target unit economics: our finance team is targeting ~ $45 / 1M tokens for generation at scale. For embeddings we are targeting ~ $10 / 1M tokens. Those are ballpark targets we need to hit to build this into our product economics.
2) Commitment preference: we prefer a 12-month reserved capacity commitment if the pricing and SLA make sense.
3) Decision timeline: procurement + infra approval in 4 weeks, final exec sign-off ~6–8 weeks.

I attached a simple token usage export that shows our monthly breakdown and projected growth. Let me know if you want a short-format PoC (we can provision a sandbox with sample data).

— Alex
Head of Platform
Acme Corp

Attachment: acme_token_report.xlsx (xls; monthly usage by workload)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Vanessa/Neha — quick internal note on pricing:
- Alex's targets ($45 gen / $10 embed) are within reason given 200M forecasted tokens. With a 12-mo reserved commit I recommend we propose:
  * Generation: $40 / 1M tokens (reserved, 12-mo commit)
  * Embeddings: $8 / 1M tokens (reserved, 12-mo commit)
- Optional: add an autoscaling burst pool (pay-as-you-go) for Q4 peaks — bill at a higher unit rate.
- Rationale: this keeps us ~20–40% below hosted-providers for equivalent quality when customers choose open-model variants + quantized execution on Dedicated. It also preserves GP by requiring a minimum commit.

I can draft a short mutual action plan and a committed pricing term sheet if you want me to.

— Marissa
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: target $/1M token benchmarking (Redwood vs OpenAI/Anthropic)

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the usage file. Based on your volume profile and preference for a 12-month commit, here is a proposed commercial we can put in an LOI/term sheet: 

Proposed commercial (12-month reserved commit):
- Generation: $40 / 1M tokens (applies to open-model variants we run on Dedicated capacity)
- Embeddings: $8 / 1M tokens
- Minimum monthly committed spend: $6,000 (can be revisited after Q2 usage review)
- Optional burst capacity: pay-as-you-go at $65 / 1M tokens for generation, $12 / 1M for embeddings (for peaks beyond committed throughput)

Benchmark note (to help with vendor comparisons):
- Redwood (Dedicated + quantized open models): target economics ~ $30–$60 / 1M gen tokens depending on model and quantization; our reserved offer here sits at $40 to be competitive and predictable.
- OpenAI hosted (latest gen): typically higher — often in the $80–$200 / 1M gen token band for advanced hosted models depending on model family and features.
- Anthropic hosted: comparable to OpenAI in many production tiers.
- Other managed open-model hosts/self-hosted providers: can be lower on unit cost but often require more ops or reduced SLAs.

Next steps:
1) If this aligns, I can have a short term sheet/LOI and mutual action plan drafted by EOD Monday and send a DocuSign link for procurement review.
2) We can schedule a 2-week PoC sandbox (we'll provide a dedicated endpoint, example prompts, and a small eval suite) — useful to validate latency and token counts.
3) Please loop in any legal compliance contact if you need SOC2 or additional evidence.

Links/attachments: pricing teaser (attached), HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4821), DocuSign placeholder (https://www.docusign.com/ctt/DEAL-4821-proposal).

Happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if procurement wants to review.

Thanks — Vanessa
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
